Alterflora

A Second Life for Natural Materials

In this project

Project briefToolsResearch methodsProcess & experimentsOutcomes — film

Project brief

Alterflora is an interactive kinetic installation that explores how digital technologies can give natural materials a second life by introducing new behavioural capabilities. Inspired by the responsive movements of living organisms, the project transforms a static wooden structure into a dynamic, responsive form. Through ultrasonic sensing and motor-driven actuation, the wooden flower opens and closes in response to human proximity, creating a subtle interaction between the human body and the material. By integrating natural materials with digital sensing and control, Alterflora explores how passive materials can acquire new forms of movement and expression, extending their potential beyond conventional structural roles to participate in human–environment interactions.

Tools

Arduino IDE, ROS 2

Research methods

Material Experimentation, Kinetic Prototyping, Interaction Testing
